propositions: The caused_by auto-derivation mechanism uses git blame over impacted file paths to attribute closed bugs when no explicit cause is supplied via --caused-by flag.
Among 88 closed bugs carrying caused_by edges, the real derive_caused_by reproduced 38 edges consistently (43%), disagreed on 6 (7%), and abstained on 44 (50% with documented failure reasons).
For 8 bugs with independently proven root causes, the deriver abstained on 7 and produced one wrong-target attribution naming an innocent producer whose code was correct at write time.
The recorded caused_by edges carry no provenance marker distinguishing blame-derived from explicitly supplied attributions, making it impossible to bulk-verify which edges are guesses versus proven.
The fail-closed abstention pattern (50% population, 7/8 subsample) indicates the strict majority-rule design is working as intended for hard defect shapes like unmet obligations and carrier commits.

A derived-vs-explicit provenance field on the link event would enable consumers to weight or exclude guesses while preserving harmless agreements, and is the recommended remedy rather than deriver logic changes.
